## Wabash National Corporation (WNC) `Transportation Equipment`
- WNC closed at **$14.04**, up **12.68%** on Friday, October 2, 2026; the quoted after-hours price was **$14.03**, down **0.07%**, at **16:01 ET**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct 2 16:01 ET)[5]
- A market-mover report attributed WNC’s **6.4%** intraday rise to weaker-than-expected September U.S. employment data: payrolls increased by **29,000** versus the **84,000** consensus, unemployment rose to **4.2%**, and Treasury yields fell after the release. (Yahoo Finance/StockStory, Oct 2 19:46 ET)[2]
- The same report said lower borrowing costs could reduce financing costs for buyers of heavy equipment, and listed **Avis Budget Group +3.6%**, **Novanta +4.2%**, **FuelCell Energy +6.8%**, and **Nextpower +5.0%** among stocks rising in the session. (Yahoo Finance/StockStory, Oct 2 19:46 ET)[2]
- WNC’s latest reported quarter showed a **$0.53 loss per share** versus a **$0.56 consensus loss**, and revenue of **$417.24 million** versus a **$402.85 million consensus**; revenue declined **9.1% year over year**. (MarketBeat, Oct 2 2026)[1]
- Wabash had reported a Q2 2026 backlog of **$956 million**, up **14.0%** from the prior quarter; Q2 revenue was **$417.24 million**, down **9.06% year over year**, with a **$25.30 million operating loss** and **$22.61 million net loss**. (Ad Hoc News, Oct 1 2026; updated Oct 2)[4]
- Wabash’s Q3 2026 outlook called for revenue of **$440 million–$460 million** and adjusted diluted loss per share of **$0.40–$0.50**. (Ad Hoc News, Oct 1 2026; updated Oct 2)[4]
- DA Davidson reiterated a **Buy** rating and a **$20.00** price target on September 22, 2026; the reported analyst consensus was **Hold**, with an average target of **$21.67**. (MarketBeat, Oct 2 2026)[1]
- Wabash declared a quarterly cash dividend of **$0.08 per share**, with an ex-dividend date of **October 8, 2026**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct 3 12:24 ET)[5]
- On October 5, Wabash announced that its Q3 2026 earnings conference call would be held on **October 29, 2026 at 12:00 ET**; the announcement did not provide new financial results or guidance. (GlobeNewswire, Oct 5 10:58 ET)[11]
- No company-specific catalyst published within the window was identified beyond the earnings, backlog, dividend, and scheduled-call information above; the clearest reported explanation for the October 2 move was the broader post-employment-report decline in Treasury yields and lower financing-cost expectations. (Yahoo Finance/StockStory, Oct 2 19:46 ET)[2]
